src.label: ANSVSA (Romanian food safety and veterinary authority) — guide on non-commercial movement of pets (PDF)

head: Up to 5 pets may travel with you; a pet from a non-EU country needs a veterinary certificate to the EU model.
lines: The ANSVSA guide sets the conditions for bringing third-country pets into Romania under its Order 98/2015 and EU Regulation 576/2013. A dog, cat or ferret from a country that is not on the special passport lists must carry the veterinary certificate for non-commercial movement into the EU.

Non-commercial movement means at most 5 pets with the owner or an authorised person, none meant for sale or transfer. More than 5 is allowed only for a competition, show or sports event, with written proof and animals older than six months.

A pet may travel up to 5 days before or after its owner, if the owner signs a declaration naming the person responsible. A pet that does not meet the conditions is not admitted; it can be sent back or put in quarantine until it does, and as a last resort be put down, at the owner's cost.
